Consult Summary:
• 37-year-old individual with known eczema presents via telehealth with a 3-day worsening flare of widespread pruritic, erythematous, dry dermatitis affecting chest, arms, hands, and antecubital fossae; no signs of infection; plan for stronger topical steroid (Betnovate), oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine), and continuation of emollients with review in 2 weeks.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Rapidly worsening, sore, red, itchy, and dry rash.
• Onset/Duration: “Past few days”; progressive worsening.
• Distribution: Chest, hands, arms, especially inside elbows (worst area); “all over my body” but emphasis on flexural areas.
• Character: Pruritic, erythematous, dry; cracks present; no weeping, no lichenification, no excoriations.
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: None identified; usual emollients not relieving.
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, joint pains, systemic symptoms.
• Past episodes: Previous eczema; current flare described as “way worse.”
• Review of systems: Negative for fever, joint pain, respiratory symptoms (other than baseline asthma), or new systemic complaints.

Past Medical History:
• Atopic eczema – recurrent; currently flared.
• Asthma – intermittent, uses blue (salbutamol) inhaler PRN; no daily controller noted.
• No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
• Diprobase cream – topical emollient; dose/route/frequency not documented (patient uses daily).
• Dermol wash – topical emollient cleanser; dose/route/frequency not documented (patient uses in shower).
• Hydrocortisone 1% cream (OTC) – topical; ineffective for current flare.
• Salbutamol “blue inhaler” – inhaled PRN for asthma; dose/frequency not documented.
• Tried OTC cetirizine previously – ineffective.
• Newly prescribed today:
  – Fexofenadine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  – Betnovate (betamethasone valerate) cream: apply thin layer (≈ one fingertip unit) twice daily for 2 weeks.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Location: London; in secure setting for consult.
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational substances: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Mother – migraine.
• Mother – hypothyroidism (patient statement); hyperthyroidism (physician repeat) – conflict noted.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (video consultation); no vitals provided.
• Patient subjectively afebrile and well.

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute exacerbation of chronic eczema (widespread, pruritic, non-infected)
  • Plan:
    – Start Betnovate (topical betamethasone valerate) thinly BID x 2 weeks.
    – Begin oral Fexofenadine for itch control.
    – Continue current emollients (Diprovase cream, Dermol wash) liberally.
    – Educate on fingertip-unit dosing, sparing use of potent steroid.
    – Counsel on signs of secondary infection or adverse reaction; seek care promptly if occurs.
    – Tele-follow-up in 2 weeks or earlier if worsening/no improvement.

Issue 2: Asthma – stable, intermittent
  • Plan:
    – Continue PRN salbutamol inhaler.
    – No change to therapy; reinforce to seek review if frequency increases.

General plan items:
  • Prescriptions sent electronically to Boots pharmacy.
  • No routine labs/imaging indicated today.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: objective physical exam, vital signs, full medication reconciliation (doses/frequencies), allergy confirmation beyond medications (e.g., latex, foods), smoking/alcohol history.
• Internal conflict: Family history – patient states mother has “hypothyroidism,” physician restates “hyperthyroidism.” (conflict noted).
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor overlaps but clinically adequate.
